items.title: [djust] djust: Arbitrary absolute-path file read in the find_handlers_for_template MCP tool
items.summary: Affected version / file / lineVersion: djust v1.1.4 (latest release, published 2026-09-23). File: python/djust/mcp/server.py:354-433 (MCP tool find_handlers_for_template). Confirmed identical on the commit used for triage, a7e4fafd1667b4db0b1465652d4a63cb17117a07.Description@mcp.tool()def find_handlers_for_template(template_path: str) -> str:    """    Args:        template_path: Either a logical template name (e.g.            'demos/counter.html' — what you'd pass to `render`) OR            an absolute filesystem path. Both are searched.    """    ...    resolved_path: str | None = None    if os.path.isabs(template_path) and os.path.isfile(template_path):        resolved_path = template_path    else:        ...  # logical-name resolution via Django's template loader    ...    with open(resolved_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:        source = f.read()    handler_names_in_template = sorted({m.group(2) for m in dj_event_attr_re.finditer(source)})When template_path is an absolute path to an existing file, it is used directly, with no confinement to the project/template directories — no realpath() + prefix check, no allowlist. open(resolved_path, ...) then reads the file.This is inconsistent with the sibling tool in the same file (loaddata, ~line 290-303), which explicitly rejects paths outside the project directory for its own path-like parameter:candidate = os.path.realpath(...)if base_dir and not candidate.startswith(os.path.realpath(str(base_dir))):    return json.dumps({"error": f"fixture path '{p}' resolves outside the project directory", ...})find_handlers_for_template has no equivalent check for template_path before the open() call.ImpactAn MCP client with access to this tool (available whenever the Django project is running the MCP server via python manage.py djust_mcp — no separate opt-in flag gates this specific tool beyond that) can read the contents of any file on disk that the process has read permission to and that exists, by passing an absolute path — e.g. /etc/passwd, application .env files, SSH keys, or any other sensitive file reachable by the server process's user.Mitigating factor (reduces this from High to Medium): the tool does not return the raw file content. It runs one fixed regex (dj-(?:click|submit|change|input|keydown|keyup)\s*=\s*'"['"]) against the content and returns only the matched handler-name strings, plus confirmation that the file exists and is readable (an existence/readability oracle on its own, independent of the regex match). If the targeted file happens to contain text matching that HTML-attribute-like pattern (plausible for config files, logs, or any text file with key="value"-shaped content), those substrings are returned in full — so the read is not purely blind, but it is not a general-purpose arbitrary-file-read primitive either.Proof of Concept / ReproductionTraced via direct source read; no live Django project was exercised for this report (would require a full djust project scaffold, which was out of scope for this pass — see limitation below).MCP client calls: find_handlers_for_template(template_path="/etc/passwd")server.py ~line 393:   if os.path.isabs(template_path) and os.path.isfile(template_path):       resolved_path = template_pathserver.py ~line 430:   with open(resolved_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:       source = f.read()sourceThe regex dj_event_attr_re.finditer(source) is applied to the real/etc/passwd content. /etc/passwd will not match this specific pattern, sothe response would report an empty handler list plus "file exists and wasread" - which already confirms the path-confinement bypass (compare withpassing a nonexistent absolute path, which correctly returns"Template file not found").On a target where the absolute path points to a file that DOES containtext shaped like dj-click="..." (e.g. a copied HTML fragment, a strayconfig value, or a crafted file placed by the attacker via anothervector), the matched substrings are returned verbatim in the JSONresponse - full-content disclosure of just those substrings, not thewhole file.Suggested FixApply the same confinement loaddata already uses, before the os.path.isfile check:if os.path.isabs(template_path):    candidate = os.path.realpath(template_path)    if base_dir and not candidate.startswith(os.path.realpath(str(base_dir))):        return json.dumps({            "error": f"template path '{template_path}' resolves outside the project directory",            "resolved": candidate,            "project_dir": str(base_dir),        })    if os.path.isfile(candidate):        resolved_path = candidateLimitationsNot exercised against a live Django/djust project — this is a source-level trace of the exact executed branch (os.path.isabs + os.path.isfile + open()), not an end-to-end runtime capture.Did not verify whether any MCP-host-level confirmation/approval step (some MCP clients prompt the user before a tool call with a suspicious-looking path argument) would

items.title: [pypdf] pypdf: Possible infinite loop in PdfWriter.find_outline_item
items.summary: ImpactAn attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to an infinite loop. This requires calling find_outline_item on a PdfWriter.PatchesThis has been fixed in pypdf==6.20.1.WorkaroundsIf you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR #4188.Referenceshttps://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/security/advisories/GHSA-qfv9-64jg-mh7phttps://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4188https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/commit/c9c35b4471c2eb5fe078094f6c816e69d4ed25a0https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.20.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qfv9-64jg-mh7p

items.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv bash activate runs commands from an environment name with a backslash before $
items.summary: SummaryThe bash activate script escapes the environment name for only one of the two passes bash makes over PS1, so abackslash in the name undoes the escaping and a name containing \$(...) runs as commands in the user's shell eachtime bash draws the prompt.Affected areasrc/virtualenv/activation/bash/activate.sh, the block that prepends the environment name to PS1.Attacker-controlled inputThe environment name: the environment directory's name, or the --prompt or VIRTUALENV_PROMPT value. An attackerneeds to influence it, for example through a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through,or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive. --prompt . takes the current directory's name.Detailsbash handles PS1 in two passes each time it draws the prompt: it first decodes backslash prompt escapes, turning \\into \ and \$ into $ (or # for root), and then runs parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmeticexpansion on the result. Since 21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in the name, but onlyfor the second pass, so the decode pass strips the escaping that a backslash in the name precedes. Releases before21.13.0 do not escape the name at all. A bash running as root decodes \$ to #, so the payload shows the wrong textthere but runs nothing. zsh does no decode pass and is not affected.Proof of concept$ virtualenv --prompt 'a\$(touch PWNED)' env$ bash --norc --noprofile -c 'source env/bin/activate; printf "%s" "${PS1@P}"'$ ls PWNEDPWNEDImpactArbitrary command execution in the shell of a user who sources the activate script of an environment whose name anattacker influenced, with that user's privileges, once per prompt draw.Versions tested21.14.6 with bash 5.2.15 on Debian bookworm, as an unprivileged user and as root.Known mitigationSet VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1 before you source activate, which leaves PS1 alone, or run shopt -u promptvarsif your prompt does not need expansion. Check the name of an environment you did not create before you source itsactivate.Latest release The problem reproduces on the latest virtualenv release.21.14.6PatchesFixed in 21.14.7. Under bash, activate now escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks for both passes, so theexample above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh keeps the single escaping it needs.Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/c3104e02474b652832a9bbaae79f6e1696296932CreditsFound while running the virtualenv test suite as root inside the Anthropic OSS Scanner build image.Referenceshttps://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-vxj4-q4g9-crj7https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113725https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/c3104e02474b652832a9bbaae79f6e1696296932https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/releases/tag/21.14.7https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vxj4-q4g9-crj7

items.title: [pypdf] pypdf: Possible large memory usage for streams with multiple filters
items.summary: ImpactAn attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large memory consumption. This requires accessing any stream with a large amount of filters or multiple filters which pass around large amounts of data.PatchesThis has been fixed in pypdf==6.20.0.WorkaroundsIf you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR #4173.Referenceshttps://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/security/advisories/GHSA-7mh2-4gg2-979fhttps://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4173https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/commit/80a84d4be6022d910874ccb0d2365400f3f0e185https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.20.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mh2-4gg2-979f

items.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv activate runs commands from the environment name in zsh with PROMPT_SUBST
items.summary: Impactzsh users activate an environment with the bash activate script, which puts the environment name into PS1. Since21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in that name, but only when BASH_VERSION is set, sozsh gets the raw value. With the PROMPT_SUBST option set, zsh runs parameter expansion, command substitution andarithmetic expansion on PS1 each time it draws the prompt. A name that contains $(...), backticks or ${...} thenruns as commands in the user's shell, once per prompt.The name comes from the environment directory, or from --prompt or VIRTUALENV_PROMPT. After you create anenvironment with:$ virtualenv 'x$(touch PWNED)y'source 'x$(touch PWNED)y/bin/activate' in a zsh session with PROMPT_SUBST set creates PWNED, and the prompt shows(xy). Passing that value as --prompt to an environment with a plain name has the same effect. WithoutPROMPT_SUBST, zsh shows the name as text and runs nothing. bash runs nothing either.A plain zsh starts with PROMPT_SUBST off. oh-my-zsh users have it on: oh-my-zsh loadslib/theme-and-appearance.zshat startup, and that file sets it. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrappertool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.--prompt . takes the current directory's name.zsh also reads % in PS1 as a prompt escape, so a name with %n showed the user name in place of those characters,though without running commands.The bug is in releases up to and including 21.14.3. The payload runs on 20.26.6 and 21.14.3, and the reporter confirmed21.9.1.PatchesFixed in 21.14.4. Under zsh, activate now escapes the name the way it does under bash and doubles%, so the example above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh gets the escaping even whenPROMPT_SUBST is off, because a user can set the option after activation; a name with a backslash, dollar sign orbacktick then shows the added backslashes.Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/5b915367da82bd024b2a0d28d2f98007034b4aa2WorkaroundsSet VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1 before you source activate, which leaves PS1 alone, or rununsetopt prompt_subst if your prompt does not need it. Check the name of an environment you did not create before yousource its activate.CreditsKaya Emre Arikan (@kemrec) reported this issue.Referenceshttps://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-5vjq-rrrf-7h2qhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113726https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/5b915367da82bd024b2a0d28d2f98007034b4aa2https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/releases/tag/21.14.4https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5vjq-rrrf-7h2q

items.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv activate.fish runs commands from a path or prompt with a backslash before a quote
items.summary: ImpactFishActivator defines no quote(), so it inherits ViaTemplateActivator.quote, which returns shlex.quote(string). That function follows POSIX sh rules, where a backslash inside single quotes stays a literal character. fish reads \' inside single quotes as an escaped quote and \\ as an escaped backslash. A value with a backslash before a quote therefore ends the literal somewhere other than where shlex.quote put the end, and fish expands the command substitution that follows.The environment path reaches set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV, and --prompt or VIRTUALENV_PROMPT reaches set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT. For --prompt "x\'\$(touch PWNED)'\'", the generated activate.fish contains:set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT 'x\'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'\'"'"''source bin/activate.fish runs touch PWNED, and fish prints no error. The same payload as a directory name runs through VIRTUAL_ENV. --prompt . takes the current directory's name, so running virtualenv inside a directory someone else named is enough. Without the backslash the payload runs nothing, and under bash it runs nothing either.virtualenv generates activate.fish by default. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.The bug affects every release up to 21.14.1 that ships activate.fish. The GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2 fix in 21.7.13 moved the placeholders outside their quotes but kept shlex.quote.PatchesFixed in 21.14.2. activate.fish now escapes backslashes and single quotes the way fish reads them, so the example above runs nothing and shows the prompt as given. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/3bddeaf8d02c3ee7f576503efb082f8f494cfcabWorkaroundsDo not create an environment whose path or prompt contains a backslash, and inspect activate.fish before you source one you did not create.CreditsKevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.Referenceshttps://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-c947-3pg5-gm8qhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113732https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/3bddeaf8d02c3ee7f576503efb082f8f494cfcabhttps://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/releases/tag/21.14.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c947-3pg5-gm8q

items.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv activation scripts run code from a path that contains a placeholder name
items.summary: ImpactViaTemplateActivator.instantiate_template replaces the placeholders in an activation template one key at a time, each across the whole text. When a value that it already substituted and quoted contains the name of a later placeholder, the later pass rewrites that name inside the quoted literal. The inserted value brings its own quotes, which close the outer literal, and the rest of the path runs as code when a user activates the environment.__VIRTUAL_NAME__ holds the environment's directory name, so a destination such as A__VIRTUAL_NAME__B/x'$(touch PWNED)'y is enough. In the default activate for bash, the VIRTUAL_ENV line renders as:VIRTUAL_ENV='/tmp/t/A'x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y'B/x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y'Sourcing that script runs touch PWNED. The same payload in a path without the placeholder name runs nothing. activate.fish runs the command the same way, and the reporter also showed Python code execution through activate.xsh and bin/activate_this.py. In activate.csh, a directory named after a prompt display placeholder, such as __VIRTUAL_PROMPT_DISPLAY_TCSH__, breaks the script with Unmatched '''.No change to quote() can stop this, because the rewrite happens after quote() ran; it defeats shlex.quote and repr() alike.An attacker needs to influence the destination path or --prompt: a CI job or wrapper tool that builds the path from a branch or project name, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.The bug affects versions 20.26.6 through 21.14.1. Version 20.26.6 first quoted template values (#2768) and introduced the per-key loop.PatchesFixed in 21.14.2. Activation scripts now keep a placeholder name in the environment's path or prompt as plain text, and activating the example above runs nothing. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/602b26623a724827ff171bf11fef4ad186d01f74WorkaroundsDo not create an environment whose path or --prompt contains a placeholder name such as __VIRTUAL_NAME__, __VIRTUAL_ENV__ or __VIRTUAL_PROMPT__, and inspect the generated activation script before you source one you did not create.CreditsKevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.Referenceshttps://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-8rjx-v5ww-45pphttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113776https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/602b26623a724827ff171bf11fef4ad186d01f74https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/releases/tag/21.14.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8rjx-v5ww-45pp
